chunks: I heard him saying: The rider should give salam upon the walker, and the walker upon the seated one; and when a group meets a group, the fewer should give salam upon the more; and when one person meets a group, the single individual should give salam upon the group.

key_terms.الرَّاكِبُ: The rider; one mounted on an animal or vehicle
key_terms.الْأَقَلُّ: The fewer; the smaller group in a meeting
key_terms.الْقَاعِدُ: The seated one; one who is stationary and sitting
key_terms.الْمَاشِي: The walker; one traveling on foot
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: Gives salam; initiates the Islamic greeting 'al-salamu alaykum'

ai.seo_question: Who should initiate the Islamic greeting according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchy for initiating the Islamic greeting (salam). This ruling reflects the principle that the person in a position of greater ease or movement (rider, walker, individual) bears the obligation to initiate the greeting toward those who are less mobile or more numerous. This hadith is part of Islamic etiquette (adab) governing social interactions, reflecting the broader Quranic injunction to respond to greetings (4:86).
